bracket: [Textbook answer-key error: the key lists EIGHT lettered isomers of \(\text{C}_5\text{H}_{12}\text{O}\) but they cover only SEVEN distinct compounds, and pentan-2-ol is missing. Entry (e) is printed as \(\text{CH}_3-\text{CH}_2-\text{OH}-\text{CH}_2-\text{CH}_3\), with the \(-\text{OH}\) inserted INTO the chain — impossible as written, since oxygen there would be divalent in a carbon chain — and it is then labelled pentan-3-ol, which is already entry (d). The argument closes rather than merely suggesting: there are exactly eight straight- and branched-chain alcohols of this formula, the key names eight, two of its names are the same compound, so exactly one is absent, and enumerating them identifies it as pentan-2-ol. All eight are listed below. (The key also leaves part (ii) of this question unanswered.)]

[Textbook answer-key errors in two parts, both the same mistake — a locant tie broken the wrong way. Neither name misdescribes the compound; both simply are not the preferred IUPAC name. (ii) For \(\text{CH}_3\text{OCH}_2\text{CH}_2\text{Cl}\) both directions of numbering give the locant set \(\{1,2\}\), so the tie is broken alphabetically and \(\textit{chloro}\) takes the lower locant: 1-chloro-2-methoxyethane, not the key's 2-chloro-1-methoxyethane. (v) For the gem-dimethyl, para-ethoxy cyclohexane the two candidate sets are \(\{1,1,4\}\) and \(\{1,4,4\}\), and \(\{1,1,4\}\) is lower at the second point of difference: 4-ethoxy-1,1-dimethylcyclohexane, not the key's 1-ethoxy-4,4-dimethylcyclohexane.]

[Textbook answer-key error in part (i): the key names the compound 4-chloro-3-ethyl-2-(1-methylethyl)butan-1-ol, using a FOUR-carbon parent chain. The principal chain must be the longest one containing the carbon that bears the \(-\text{OH}\), and a five-carbon chain running through the group the key itself calls "3-ethyl" does contain it — so the correct name is 3-(chloromethyl)-2-(propan-2-yl)pentan-1-ol. The book corroborates this against itself: the exercise key's answer to Ex 7.2(x) draws this same skeleton and takes the five-carbon chain as the parent. Part (ii) agrees.]
